chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf, the Hajj of Islam, but the entirety of what he left did not reach (the required amount), except for fifty Dirhams. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should perform Hajj on his behalf from one of the junctures which Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used as a juncture (to wear Ihram), from nearby'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a deceased person leaves insufficient funds for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of proportional fulfillment (*nisab*) for Hajj when a deceased person's estate is insufficient to cover the full cost of Hajj al-Islam. The Imam specifies that the available funds should be used to perform the essential rites from a nearby miqat, ensuring the obligation is discharged to the extent of the resources. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on practicality and the validity of partial performance in fulfilling bequests for the deceased.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahmoun, from Ibn Raib,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who bequeaths that Hajj be performed on his behalf, the Hajj of Al-Islam, but the entirety of what he left did not reach (the required amount), except for fifty Dirhams. Heasws said: ‘He should perform Hajj on his behalf from one of the junctures which Rasool-Allahsaww used as a juncture (to wear Ihraam), from nearby’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab who has said the following:

“About a man who dies and in his will says to perform Hajjahta al-Islam for him, but his legacy is not sufficient. It is altogether fifty dirham. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It must be performed for him from any one of the Miqat (place for assuming the state of Ihram) from which the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, assumed the state of Ihram.’”
